newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran medical workers temporarily end strike.
newsitem.headline: Honduran medical workers temporarily end strike.

text.p: Honduran health workers on Friday temporarily halted a 9-day-old strike that had virtually paralysed hospitals and health centres.
About 14,000 health workers agreed to return to work while they continued talks with the government over demands for a pay raise and a cut in prices of public sector goods.
The strike hit 28 hospitals and more than 500 health centres in this impoverished Central American nation.

"We have normalised services in all the hospitals and health centres in the country to negotiate our demands for a salary increase with a high-level government commission," Henry Echeverria, an official with the National Medical Workers' Union, told Reuters.
On Wednesday, about 10 protesters and five police were injured when riot police firing tear gas clashed with workers who stormed the Health Ministry and briefly held Health Minister Enrique Samayoa.
Police dislodged some 300 protesters from the building and rescued Samayoa unharmed.
